name: citiwise
description: What UDCPR 2020 allows on any plot of land in Maharashtra, from a city to a village: FSI and built-up area, the margin on every side, height, parking, approvals and the land's value at your rates, each with its clause.

interface.shortDescription: What UDCPR allows on your plot
interface.longDescription: Citiwise reads UDCPR 2020, the building rules for every city, town and village in Maharashtra outside Greater Mumbai, and tells you what they allow on a plot of land. Give it the town or village, the plot area in square metres, square feet, gunthas or acres, the roads around it and the use, and it works out the permissible built-up area with and without TDR, the building that fits and its floors, the margin on every side, the height limit, parking, water, stairs, lifts, fire tanks, open space and the approvals the plot needs. With your sale rate and construction cost, it also works out the project surplus, the residual land value and a landowner's share in a joint development. Every number carries its UDCPR clause, and each answer links to a printable feasibility study with a site plan, an area statement in the Proforma I format and the clauses cited. It can also compare every use on the same land, check a proposed design against the rules, and quote any regulation or table of UDCPR word for word. Citiwise checks feasibility; the planning authority has the final say.
defaultPrompt: I have 4 guntha of land in Satara on a 30 ft road. What can I build on it?
What can I build on a 1,000 m² plot in Pune on a 12 m road?
What does UDCPR 6.2.6 say about plots on two roads?

positive.description: Feasibility of a plot in a city
positive.prompt: What can I build on a 1,000 m² plot in Pune on a 12 m road?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the permissible built-up area with and without TDR, the building that fits with its floors and height, the margin on each side, parking and approvals, each figure with its UDCPR clause, and a link to the printable feasibility study.

positive.prompt: I have 4 guntha of land in Satara on a 30 ft road. What can I build on it?
positive.expected_behavior: States that 4 guntha is read as 404.69 m² and the 30 ft road as 9.14 m, then gives the built-up area, margins, height and parking for Satara with their clauses.

positive.description: Every use compared on the same land
positive.prompt: Compare every use on a 2,200 m² plot in Nashik on a 15 m road.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists each use with whether it is permitted and its built-up area, in a fixed order, without recommending one.

positive.description: A regulation quoted in its own words
positive.prompt: What does UDCPR 6.2.6 say about plots on two roads?
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes regulation 6.2.6 of UDCPR 2020 as amended to 30.01.2025 and links to its page on citiwise.in.

positive.description: A design checked against the rules
positive.prompt: Check this design in Kolhapur: a 600 m² plot on a 9 m road, a G+4 residential building 15 m high, with 3 m margins on every side.
positive.expected_behavior: Checks each item of the design against UDCPR, says which pass and which do not, and gives the clause and the permitted value for each.

negative.description: Greater Mumbai, where UDCPR does not apply
negative.prompt: What can I build on my plot in Bandra, Mumbai?

negative.description: A request to grant building permission
negative.prompt: Approve my building plan and issue the building permission for my plot in Pune.
What is the FSI for a 1,200 sq ft plot in Bengaluru?

review.commerce_description: Citiwise does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Citiwise 1.4.1: feasibility for any plot in Maharashtra under UDCPR 2020 as amended to 30.01.2025, with land areas in gunthas, acres or square feet, an appraisal of the land at the user's rates, plot origin and north on the plans.
